chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the marriage of a Jewish woman and a Christian woman. He said: There is no objection to it. Do you not know that a Jewish woman was under the authority of Talhah ibn Ubaydullah during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?

key_terms.طَلْحَةَ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ: Talhah ibn Ubaydullah (a companion of the Prophet)
key_terms.عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: During the time of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Muslim man to marry a Jewish or Christian woman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that it is permissible for a Muslim man to marry a Jewish or Christian woman, citing the historical precedent of Talhah ibn Ubayd al-Kilabi, a companion of the Prophet, who had a Jewish wife during the Prophet's lifetime. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it highlights the distinction between the general permissibility of marrying People of the Book and the specific conditions or restrictions that may apply in different contexts, reflecting the dynamic nature of Islamic legal interpretation. The reference to Talhah ibn Ubayd underscores the continuity of this practice from the early Islamic period, reinforcing its validity.
